desc: Set up this Mac for Dozer Sandbox (once): check it, choose and confirm Access (the Claude account, GitHub, the SSH agent), choose what workspace rules do, write the settings, prepare images in the background.
Make a folder a Dozer Sandbox project: write doz_project.yaml there (onboarding this Mac first if it never was).
Remove Dozer Sandbox from this Mac: the store, the settings and the installed doz — listed first, asked once.
Look for a newer doz on your channel and install it (Homebrew: brew upgrade; a tarball install: the signed download) — asks first; -y does not.
The quickest way in: a new sandbox with every default — created, started and attached.
Create a sandbox (it stays off until start or up).
Create the sandbox if it is missing, start or wake it, then attach (vagrant up / compose up).
Boot a sandbox — or wake it, if it is asleep; resume it if paused.
Pause: guest CPU to 0 in ~1 ms, RAM kept.
Resume after pause (from sleep it wakes).
Sleep: pause + snapshot to disk; RAM kept, and it survives a host crash.
Hibernate: snapshot to disk and stop the VM — RAM returned; sessions come back on wake.
Wake from sleep or hibernation (~0.3 s), sessions and pids where they were.
Shut down: a cold stop that keeps the disk; running programs end.
Reset to the image: shut down and discard the disk (restore points and the state disk stay).
Remove a sandbox and everything it has on disk.
List the sandboxes: phase, RAM held, disk, sessions, network.
Everything about a sandbox, as JSON (--prompt: the agent's environment prompt, as its next session gets it).
The sandbox's terminal sessions: list them (the default), end one, or restart one.
End a session's program: it is hung up (as when its terminal closes), then terminated, then killed if it must be.
The sandbox's terminal sessions (they survive pause, sleep and hibernate).
Restart a session: end its program and start the same one again, in the same folder.
Attach this terminal to a session (a paused or sleeping sandbox is woken).
Open a NEW session running a program, and attach to it.
Run a command in the sandbox, non-interactively; its output and exit code pass through.
Images: the built-in lab, claude-code and pi, and custom images saved from restore points.
Restore points: instant disk-only copies (APFS clones) to go back to or fork from.
What a sandbox's agent may do (its permissions), its raw policy and its connection log.
Credentials held by the host's proxy — the sandbox only ever sees a placeholder.
Accounts the host holds for sandboxes: the Mac's Claude login, setup tokens, API keys; for Codex, a ChatGPT sign-in or an OpenAI key.
Lifecycle timings recorded by the host: per action count, median, p90, min, max, failures.
Check this Mac and the store: macOS, Apple silicon, the entitlement, the kernel, vmnet, disk, the host.
The per-user host that owns every running sandbox (started for you; exits when idle).
Follow what the host does: phases, timed steps, notes (Ctrl-C stops).
Show a sandbox's boot console (the kernel and init); --follow keeps printing it as it boots (Ctrl-C stops).
The recommended bases a sandbox's image is made from (an image is a base × an agent).
List the recommended bases: the image each follows, its download, the registries its sandboxes reach, which agents' images are prepared.
Apple's container tool, which builds Dockerfile bases (installed on demand; its services started only when you say so).
Whether Apple's container tool is installed, supported and running.
Start Apple's container services (container system start --enable-kernel-install) — asks first.
Install Apple's container tool: its signed package (pinned, sha256-checked) opened in macOS Installer — asks first; never sudo.
List the images and whether each is baked in this store (--tree: the lineage, with sizes).
Bake (or rebuild) a built-in image now (otherwise the first start does it; minutes, needs network).
Remove an image's baked disk (sandboxes cloned from it keep working).
Pull an image from a registry (not yet).
Push an image to a registry (not yet).
Take a restore point (a running sandbox pauses for the clone: milliseconds).
The sandbox's restore points, oldest first.
Shut down and go back to a restore point (a "before revert" point is taken first).
A new sandbox whose disks are a restore point's (it cold-boots on start).
Delete a restore point (any, in any order).
Save a restore point (or the stopped sandbox's disk) as a custom image other sandboxes can start from.
What the agent can do: its permissions as a checklist, its sites, and what it was refused lately (the default: doz net NAME).
Switch permissions on (install:python, web, update, …; install = every ecosystem), allow a site (site:api.example.com), or set a preset (standard, locked, open).
Switch permissions off (web, update, install:node, …) or deny a site (site:HOST).
Every permission, what it means, and the hosts behind it (this doz's).
Show the policy, or change it live (the next connection is judged by it; it is kept for the next start).
The connection log (metadata only: host, verdict, rule, bytes — never contents).
Give a proxied sandbox a key: read from stdin (or a prompt) or the keychain — never an argument.
Forget a key.
Which keys a sandbox has (never their values).
What the proxy does with a credential the guest supplies itself: allow (and flag), strict (refuse), or auto.
The accounts (never a secret).
Add an account: a setup token or an API key (prompt or stdin), another Claude config dir's Mac login, a ChatGPT sign-in or an OpenAI key (Codex).
Check an account: one tiny request to api.anthropic.com (or api.openai.com for an OpenAI key); a ChatGPT sign-in is renewed when it is due.
Remove an account and the keychain item doz made for it.
The account sandboxes that follow the default use (or none).
Which account a sandbox uses: a name, default (follow the store's), or none.
on: near expiry, while a sandbox uses a Mac login and no Claude Code runs on the Mac, the host runs the Mac's claude once (off by default).
Every credential sandboxes can use — the Claude account, GitHub as you, the SSH agent — confirmed live; set a choice.
Show each credential choice and confirm it works now (the default: doz access).
Change an Access choice (the defaults for new sandboxes) and confirm it — failures are said, never blocking.
A sandbox's tools layer: the tools Dozer manages from its settings, why, and their state (--apply: set them up again now).
Workspace rules: what a .dozignore / .dozreadonly in a sandbox's workspace folder does, and why.
Which rule decides each path — locked, hidden, read-only or visible — and from which line of which file.
A sandbox's workspace rules: every pattern with its line, the mode, warnings, and whether the view runs in the sandbox.
Start the host (detached, unless --foreground).
Hibernate every running sandbox and stop the host (the next command starts a new one; wake brings each back).
Stop the host (running sandboxes hibernate) and start it again — on this doz's build (after an update).
Is a host running, and what does it hold?
After an upgrade: is a host of an older build still running?
A local web dashboard for this store: sandboxes, sessions, terminals, images, restore points, network, accounts, metrics, events.
A new one-use link to the running UI of this store (opened, or printed with --print-url).
Restart the running UI of this store — the same port (or a changed ui.port), open pages stay signed in and reconnect by themselves.
Start the UI (the default) — or, when one runs for this store, open a new link to it.
Stop the running UI of this store (a detached one, or one in another terminal); its open pages say it stopped.
The dashboard for your other computers, tablets and phones: http://<this Mac>.local:7443 on your network.
The browsers let in: name, when first and last seen, from where, which browser.
What the other browsers did (the audit log): admissions, changes, terminals, refusals.
Give a browser a name you will recognise ("Kitchen iPad").
Remove a browser (by its ID from doz serve devices), or --all: it is signed out at once and needs a new invite.
An invite for one more browser: a QR code, a short code and a link (each works once, for five minutes).
Start serving (the default) — or, when doz serve runs for this store, say where.
Whether doz serve runs for this store, where, and how many browsers are let in.
Stop the running doz serve of this store (its browsers stay let in for the next one).
Templates: a sandbox's root disk saved as an image other sandboxes are created from (never its state disk).
Save a sandbox's root disk (now, or a restore point's) as a template.
The templates in this store.
Remove a template (sandboxes created from it keep working).
A new sandbox from an existing one's disk (or a restore point), with a new workspace, CPUs, memory, network or account.
Settings: the doz.toml file, every value and where it came from (flag, env, file or default).
Every setting: its effective value and its source (the default).
One setting's effective value (--json adds its source and default).
Set one setting in the file (checked against its type and range).
Put one setting back to its default (comment it out in the file).
Write the settings file: every setting with its default commented out (an existing file keeps its values and gains any new settings).
Where the settings file is (${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/dozer-sandbox/doz.toml).
Everything Dozer uses (disk to the byte, memory, CPUs, network) and deleting what can go.
The account: every byte of the store on a row (the last row, unattributed, is ~0), then memory, CPUs, traffic and kernels.
Delete resources by id (doz resources lists them): shows what goes, what it frees and what each costs later, then asks once.
Delete what is re-creatable AND unused: the download cache, base disks, old kernels, images no sandbox was created from lately, leftovers.
The kernel NEW sandboxes boot: a kernel:<version> doz resources lists, or pinned (this build's).
